svg.title: DDIA 4 · STORAGE & RETRIEVAL: sketchnote
svg.text: Two engine families: log-structured (append, LSM) and page-oriented (update
in place, B-tree). Analytics wants columns; search wants special indexes.
Old values pile up, so background compaction merges segments
and keeps only the latest value per key.
A read checks the memtable, then SSTables from newest to
oldest. Bloom filters skip files that can't contain the key, so
~10 bits per key → ~1% false "maybe", never a false "no". Lets
Updates overwrite the page in place, after writing to the WAL
first so a crash mid-write can be repaired. A full page splits in
Key may exist in many files, so
Key in one place: easy range locks
"Ad clicks are write-heavy and append-only, around 10k/sec, so an LSM-based
Values in one column look alike, so they compress very well.
Vectorized CPU processing on top makes these scans 10–100×
used for semantic search and RAG · pgvector, Faiss
Embed text so similar meaning = nearby vectors. IVF searches
near clusters; HNSW walks a layered graph. Behind RAG.
"LSM-tree storage: writes are sequential appends to memtable +
commit log, so write throughput is very high.
"How do you make this query fast?"
Name the exact index: "a composite index on (user_id,
created_at DESC) turns it into a single index range scan."
Never on the OLTP primary. Use CDC or Kafka into a column
Log the change before applying it. After a crash, replay the log.
The same idea powers replication (Ch 5) and CDC (Ch 11).
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.
